mechanism_narrative: Sustained decline in RETAIL_REC over four consecutive weeks (-13.6% to -20.0%) reflects a persistent demand destruction that will continue into the next four-week period absent a reversal signal in complementary mobility series. The trend momentum carries forward.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined monotonically from -13.6% to -20.0% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the prior 28 days by more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility (17.6% to 10.7% decline in negative deviation) indicates consumers are shifting discretionary spending toward essential goods. This substitution effect suppresses RETAIL_REC demand over the next four weeks as household budgets remain constrained.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +10% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases while GROCERY_PHARM falls below +5% in the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved from -9.9% to -4.4% over four weeks, signaling partial return to office routines. This recovery in commuting activity will drive incidental retail visits during work-week transit corridors, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -5% and TRANSIT remains above +2%
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 5.5 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES falls below -8% or TRANSIT drops below 0% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated (+4.1% to +5.1%) indicating sustained stay-at-home behavior driven by policy restrictions or health concerns. Elevated residential presence suppresses RETAIL_REC as outdoor mobility constraints persist, maintaining negative retail momentum into the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +4% for all four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops below +2% while RETAIL_REC simultaneously increases above -10% in the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has deteriorated from -11.9% to -17.9%, indicating suppressed outdoor recreational activity. This signals either weather constraints or policy-driven closures that will also constrain retail-adjacent outdoor shopping and entertainment venues over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 6 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility recovers above -10% while RETAIL_REC remains below -15% in the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The divergence between GROCERY_PHARM resilience (+10.7%) and RETAIL_REC collapse (-20.0%) reflects a bifurcated consumer behavior: essential-goods demand remains stable while discretionary retail is severely suppressed. This structural split will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds RETAIL_REC by more than 25 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:Gap between GROCERY_PHARM (+10.7%) and RETAIL_REC (-20.0%) is 30.7 percentage points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 10 percentage points while GROCERY_PHARM falls below +5% in the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized around +2-3% over four weeks despite WORKPLACES weakness, indicating essential commuting persists. If TRANSIT remains stable and WORKPLACES continues recovery above -5%, incidental retail footfall during transit hub activities will drive RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains between +1% and +4% AND WORKPLACES rises above -5%
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stable at +2.6% in t-0w, WORKPLACES at -4.4%
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls below 0% or WORKPLACES drops below -8% in the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.

These restrictions will remain binding over the next one to two weeks, preventing RETAIL_REC recovery and maintaining negative momentum.
